newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rainfall selective in Brazil soybean areas -- coops.
newsitem.headline: Rainfall selective in Brazil soybean areas -- coops.

text.p: Rainfall remained uneven in Brazil's key soybean growing regions, leaving some areas with severe water shortages while in others the crop was developing normally, coops said.
In Parana state, it rained again overnight with between seven and 15 mm falling near Campo Mourao, according to Luis Carlos da Lima at the Coamo cooperative.
Skies were covered Friday, indicating further rain was on the way, and the soy crop was developing normally, he said.
But in the other key growing state of Rio Grande do Sul, rainfall remained patchy and temperatures high.
At the Cotriba cooperative in Ibiruba, the situation was becoming critical.
"The soybean has stopped developing because humidity is very low," said agronomist Aurio Zanatta. "We haven't had any rain since Dec 20. We need rain right away."
He added, "The danger is that when it starts raining again, the soybean will enter into the flowering stage without developing sufficiently during the vegetative phase."
In the area around Rondinha, temperatures ranged from 35 to 40 degrees Celsius and some areas had not seen any rain for five days.
"We had 20 mm of rain yesterday, but it wasn't generalized," said Volnei Zorzi of the Coorondinha cooperative. "It was in isolated showers. Some places received as little as three mm."
Between 15 and 20 percent of the area's crop was entering into the flowering stage, he added.
